questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to experience a living in a culture and climate that was very different from Denmark. It was also important to me that the country is really safe and that English is the main language.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: We received a lot of information and guides, and the administration was pretty easy to communicate with. The amount of information could get a bit overwhelming at times, but overall the process went well.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I didn't get any assistance directly from the university when i arrived, but I found it very helpful to join the NUS Exchangers WhatsApp group.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: There were a couple of different types of housing on campus. I chose to live in a house as I wanted aircon and didn't want to have a meal plan.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: I lived in PGP which has a canteen with a bunch of different food stalls. The food was pretty nice and affordable (3-5 sgd) and it was a good place to meet other exchange students. There was also a shared kitchen by my room, but you had to bring equipment and cutlery yourself. I liked not being tied to a meal plan as Singapore has a lot of interesting food options to explore.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: I was lucky to get a room with air-conditioning, but some of the other people didn't and struggled a bit with the heat. Generally I recommend trying to live on campus as it's a great way to connect with the locals and it's were I met most of my other exchange friends. It could sometimes get a bit frustrating living away from the city center, as the public transportation was comfortable but not the most efficient.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: There are a lot of different steps and deadlines which was a bit intimidating, but in the end it wasn't that difficult.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: There was a zoom presentation by NUS for exchangers where you could also ask questions. I had a technical issue at one point, but the IT support were quick to respond.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was unsuccessful in securing one of the classes I wanted, but there was a reregistration were I could choose another one. I did find that there was a relatively limited amount of sociology courses available for exchange students.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Make a little calendar with the different registration deadlines and don't overthink it too much.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I had the option of choosing courses on level 1000, 2000 and 3000. I found it nice to also have some lower level classes because it gave me more free time.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The style reminded me a bit of gymnasiet, as there was a lot of active participation throughout the semester compared to what I'm used to back home. All of my classes had tutorials, which I actually ended up really liking, because the different discussions I got to have with the local students were very interesting.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: GES1034 - We the citizens: understanding Singapore's politics, SC1101E - Making sense of society, SC2220 - Gender studies, SC3206 - Urban sociology

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Urban sociology was really interesting. A part of the final project was to do observations in different parts of the city which was fun. I also enjoyed having gender studies and getting insights into how gender is viewed in Southeast Asia.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Traveling.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Eating out and public transportation were cheaper than I expected. Buying food in grocery stores was a bit expensive, but I never cooked myself anyways.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There were a lot of different clubs, but I didn't really participate in any.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I went to a couple of events at my dorm and it was pretty fun.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Exploring different parts of the city like Chinatown, Little India and Kampong Glam. Going out at Boat Quay and participating in the different festivals/holidays. Singapore is really well connected for traveling to other countries like Malaysia and Indonesia, and a lot of the 'exchange culture' is centered around traveling.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I generally found it easy as most of the locals speak English and the multicultural nature of the country makes it feel pretty open to outsiders.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Living in campus housing gave me great opportunities to connect with local students because I was the only foreign student in my dorm cluster. Participating in the clubs would probably also have been helpful.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I found the strict laws and amount of surveillance a bit challenging at first, but I got used to it pretty quickly. The dorm also had strict rules in some areas (no alcohol or any overnight visitors) which was a bit of a culture shock. The local dialect (Singlish) could sometimes be a bit difficult to understand but it wasn't really an issue.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The food culture is amazing, I already miss the hawker centers. I also really appreciated how multicultural and safe Singapore is.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Spend as much time as you can exploring, don't worry to much about school (the grades are non transferable) and try to live on campus.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Join the NUS exchange WhatsApp group. Even though the amount of messages was a bit overwhelming, there was a lot of people exchanging useful information and arranging meetups. Be prepared for really hot and humid weather. Having a bit of cash on you is useful, as some stalls don't take credit cards. Going out is a bit expensive, but if you go out on Wednesdays (ladies night) or use the Aentry app you can save some money.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Making friends with people from a bunch of different countries and gaining new perspectives on life and the world. And getting to live in a tropical country for a whole semester :)

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: I got really sick during the exchange and had to navigate a foreign healthcare system. The NUS health center was pretty helpful though.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
